annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards. The card is described once, in cardFrom(), as ratios of its own width — and that width now comes from the FRAME rather than being declared, so the numbers the build checks reason about are the numbers that render. A breakpoint only sets the page margin and the gutter.
That is what let the cards grow into the centre rail: the gutter used to carry the 34px shadow bleed as well as the gap, and it no longer does. The clip still reaches that far, so no shadow is sliced; a soft shadow grazing a neighbour is invisible.
The row gap is now the overhang plus a little, so the second row sits close under the first without its screenshots reaching the cards above.

Page changes: the app header drops the tool links, since the cards are the navigation. The dex builder's own footer is on the bottom of every width, copied from PageFooter.tsx.
The fourth card has no gradient — there is no screenshot under the copy to rescue, and the wash only muddied the mark. Its Hammer is the app's own lucide icon, white, higher and smaller.
On desktop the card rail spans exactly the hero's measure: the left card lines up with the h1 and the right card with the sub-text's right edge, because both use the same 80px margin. The sub-text column is 700px wide so its last line holds without wrapping.
The desktop clear band is 24%: the hero, the card block and the footer together leave that much above and below.
